question.prompt: The point \(P(a,b)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is first rotated counterclockwise by \(90^\circ\) around the point \((1,5)\) and then reflected about the line \(y=-x.\) The image of \(P\) after these two transformations is at \((-6,3).\) What is \(b-a?\)

solutions.title: Undo the transformations
solutions.explanation:
Knowing the final point lets us recover \(P\) by undoing the transformations in reverse order.

Reflection across \(y=-x\) sends \((x,y)\) to \((-y,-x)\): rightward motion becomes downward motion, and upward motion becomes leftward motion. A reflection undoes itself, so the point just before the reflection was
\[
(-3,6).
\]
Relative to the rotation center \((1,5)\), this point has offset
\[
(-3-1,\,6-5)=(-4,1).
\]
To undo the counterclockwise rotation, turn this offset clockwise by \(90^\circ\). The 4 units left become 4 units up, and the 1 unit up becomes 1 unit right. The resulting offset is therefore \((1,4)\).

Adding it to the center gives
\[
P=(1+1,\,5+4)=(2,9).
\]
Thus \(a=2\), \(b=9\), and \(\boxed{b-a=7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutions.title: Track the final coordinate sum
solutions.explanation:
Writing the image coordinates in terms of \(a\) and \(b\) lets us obtain \(b-a\) directly from their sum.

The offset of \(P\) from the rotation center is \((a-1,b-5)\). A counterclockwise quarter-turn sends an offset \((u,v)\) to \((-v,u)\), because rightward motion becomes upward motion and upward motion becomes leftward motion. Adding the center back, the rotated point is
\[
\bigl(1-(b-5),\,5+(a-1)\bigr)=(6-b,a+4).
\]
Reflection across \(y=-x\) swaps the coordinates and changes both signs, since it reflects the positive coordinate-axis directions into the opposite axes. Thus the final image is
\[
(-a-4,b-6).
\]
Its coordinate sum is \(b-a-10\). The given final point \((-6,3)\) has coordinate sum \(-3\), so
\[
b-a-10=-3.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{b-a=7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
